name: Pipe Organ
desc: A pipe-organ facade — ranks of graduated metal flue pipes rising in towers and flats from a carved wooden plinth, an unseen light raking across the rank so the burnished pipes gleam in turn; stands as a centred instrument leaving margins open — burnished tin/pewter, gilded gold, deep chiaroscuro, a schematic, or an engraving.

energy.doc: how brightly the raking light gleams on the metal (master brightness)

scale.doc: pipe size — min a compact chamber organ, max a towering cathedral instrument

density.doc: how many pipes stand in the facade (12 to 28)

speed.doc: how fast the raking light sweeps the rank

sweep.doc: how far and fast the bright zone travels across the pipes

x.doc: centre of the instrument across frame

y.doc: the impost line the pipes stand on — pipes rise above it

style.doc: aesthetic: burnished tin/pewter pipes / gilded gold / deep chiaroscuro pulled out of black by the sweep / a cyan schematic / a hatched engraving plate

alpha.doc: layer opacity — scales every mark so it dissolves into the background rather than veiling it
